subject: Dedicated capacity: time-slicing guarantee addendum & queueing fairness
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@orbitalrail.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@orbitalrail.io>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Time-slicing guarantee for dedicated pool / queueing fairness

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — Orbital Rail is close to finalizing numbers for a 3-year reserved-GPU commitment, but procurement has flagged one open item: how Redwood will guarantee throughput for interactive inference during our nightly batch windows.

Our basic ask: an addendum that explicitly defines a time-slicing guarantee (nightly batch window exceptions and notification cadence) and a queueing-fairness approach when reserved GPUs are contending with burst traffic from other customers on the same scheduling domain. We are not asking to be prioritized above commitments, but we need predictable tail behavior for our interactive product during peak morning hours.

Some context:
- Reserved footprint: 16 reserved GPUs (rsv-aurora-16)
- Nightly batch window: 02:00–06:00 UTC, heavy KV-loads and long generation latencies (batch jobs)
- Interactive peak: 13:00–15:00 UTC (short queries, <200 tokens)

Can you share an example addendum or playbook that spells out:
- how queueing will be shaped between batch and interactive workloads,
- what metrics Redwood will report (percentiles, dropped/bumped requests),
- and what preemption/notice policy would look like if headroom runs out?

Procurement copied here — they want the language we’ll attach to the SOW. Can you get a draft over?

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform & Scheduling
Orbital Rail
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@orbitalrail.io>
Cc: procurement <procurement@orbitalrail.io>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Time-slicing guarantee for dedicated pool / queueing fairness

Hi Sanjay — really appreciate the context. I’ve looped in Lauren (ops policy) and Kim (service guarantees) so we can give you a concrete addendum. Attached are two working artifacts to start: a short "queueing_playbook_draft.docx" and the current "reserved_sku_terms_v2.pdf" that shows baseline reservations.

Initial answers / commitments we can include in the addendum:
- We can define a soft time-slice carveout for nightly batch windows that provides a minimum of X% of the reserved pool for interactive traffic during those windows (configurable; example values in the playbook).
- We’ll publish per-customer token-level observability during the carveout window (p50/p95/p99 latencies and a preemption count).
- Preemption policy: we provide 30 minutes of proactive notice + a targeted fallback model variant before preemption (customers can opt for longer notice in SOW).

Can we set a 30-min call Tuesday to walk procurement through the wording and the metrics we’ll publish? Lauren, Kim — would you take point on the technical carveout language and the SLO examples?

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
Attachments: reserved_sku_terms_v2.pdf; queueing_playbook_draft.docx
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@orbitalrail.io>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 Aug 2026 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Time-slicing guarantee for dedicated pool / queueing fairness

Hi all — quick technical clarifications and suggested SLO language below. I kept it concise so procurement can drop it into the SOW.

Suggested carveout model (example values — we can tune):
- Reservation: 16 GPUs (elastic within reserved pool).
- Time-sliced reserve: During specified nightly windows (02:00–06:00 UTC), Redwood will maintain an interactive headroom of 20% of reserved capacity (i.e., 3.2 GPUs worth of baseline throughput) unless customer opts out.
- Queueing behavior: Batch jobs will be admitted into a lower-priority queue and subject to fair share with a max inflight limit. Interactive traffic will have priority up to the headroom threshold; once headroom exceeded, we apply gradual request shedding with backoff signals and redirect to a compatible cheaper model variant as fallback.

Observable metrics to include in addendum:
- Per-minute concurrent in-flight requests (interactive vs batch)
- Token generation latencies (p50/p95/p99) for interactive traffic
- Preemption/redirect counts and notice timestamps
- Headroom utilization percentage

Operational guarantees / notices:
- Proactive notice of scheduled preemption: 30 minutes (email + webhook).
- Emergency preemption: immediate, but we will open a support incident and credit for any unserved SLA window as per SOW credits table.

Kim — can you confirm whether the 20% example is realistic for rsv-aurora-16 or if we should use a different baseline? Also, do we want to offer a paid option for guaranteed 40% headroom?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Platform Ops
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@orbitalrail.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@orbitalrail.io>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Time-slicing guarantee for dedicated pool / queueing fairness

Thanks Lauren — that level of detail is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Workload shape — our nightly batches are windowed (02:00–06:00 UTC) but bursty inside that window: short periods of very high KV writes followed by longer model runs. Interactive traffic is predictable but deploys heavy load during the 13:00–15:00 UTC slot.
2) We like the 20% headroom example; procurement wants the addendum to include:
   - explicit queue-depth limits for batch jobs (so they can be throttled ASAP),
   - an SLA credit table if headroom drops below the threshold more than 3 times in a 30-day rolling window, and
   - the 30-minute proactive notice requirement.

Procurement is looped for contract language. We’ll also send a short CSV of observed concurrency by hour to help you size the example X% precisely.

Sanjay
Sanjay Patel
Head of Platform & Scheduling, Orbital Rail
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, procurement <procurement@orbitalrail.io>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Time-slicing guarantee for dedicated pool / queueing fairness

Sanjay — thanks, all makes sense. Summary and next steps: 

- Redwood will draft an addendum that includes: time-slice headroom language (example 20% for rsv-aurora-16), per-customer observability metrics (p50/p95/p99), queue-depth limits for batch jobs, and a sliding SLA-credit table (trigger: >3 headroom breaches in 30 days).
- We’ll include the 30-minute proactive notice requirement verbatim.
- Internal action: Lauren & Kim to produce final wording + numeric examples; Ben to circulate draft addendum and an updated reserved_sku_terms_v2.pdf with the carveout appended.
- External action: Sanjay to send the CSV of observed concurrency so we can finalize the headroom percent.
- Proposed timeline: draft addendum by Friday (2026-08-21); review call Tuesday 2026-08-24, 10:00 UTC.

Attached artifacts: queueing_playbook_draft.docx, reserved_sku_terms_v2.pdf (see earlier). HubSpot link for the deal is https://app.redwood.ai/hubspot/ORB-2026-07; we’ll post the addendum draft there and start the DocuSign envelope once language is agreed.
